title: Listen Closely: Measuring Vocal Tone in Corporate Disclosures

scopes.description: Full supplied Python workflow: independent Table 2 and Table 3 analyses; author sample construction; and market outcomes using the constructed call-level sample plus a separate Fama-sorted portfolio panel. Includes the shared regression helper as supporting code. Tab4 and Tab5 are byte-identical copies and represent one market-outcome source path to run once.

issues.description: The package includes five analysis/preparation entry scripts and a shared helper, but only the identifier subset is packaged among the consumed analysis inputs. Required author workbook/panels, the prepared phonetics and call-level tone files, and the source procedures for several panels remain unprovided. create_sample.py writes CALL_LEVEL_SAMPLE.parquet and the market-outcome scripts read it; there is no supported complete source-to-output closure until the missing inputs and their producers are supplied.

Catalogued local CRSP.DSF and CRSP.DSF_V2 are raw security/date products whose inspected schemas do not contain callid, car_0_1, car_2_61 or t-1. The supplied code does not construct the call-linked event-window panel or document the event dates, security mapping or return-window rules. The raw candidates do not establish a compatible route, access barrier, or absence of data.

The author-prepared I/B/E/S files are call-linked panels, while catalogued raw detail, actual and statistics candidates do not supply callid and the prepared quarter dates, drift measures and split-adjusted prices. No source maps calls to I/B/E/S identifiers, selects revisions or constructs the prepared panels. Catalog results do not establish access or prove the prepared files are absent elsewhere.

The market-outcome scripts consume a study-specific quintile-sorted voice-tone panel with Fama-French factors, but the package contains no producer or schema for it. A catalog miss for a Fama-specific product is not evidence of nonexistence or access restriction.

review_notes: Source reading used the saved byte-first masking workflow. Its first fixture run exposed an off-by-one block-comment range before any author source was displayed; the original helper and result were preserved, the corrected v2 helper passed the saved fixture set, and only the v2 manifest is cited. The raw code_execution_log.log was skipped as opaque and never opened or displayed. Normal withheld markers were handled as masking, not treated as an incident. Process-only incident records E_PROCESS_READER_V1 and E_PROCESS_FIELD_V1 are preserved as unused evidence rows; neither ID appears in any evidence_ids array. Their original helper sources are preserved in probes, while scientific claims cite only the corrected v2 screen and comparison.

The first source-field comparison helper wrote intermediate artifacts but exited while serializing its compact summary because the summary used PosixPath dictionary keys. The failed helper and outputs were preserved and are not cited; the corrected v2 comparison and its eight selected full native schemas are the cited records.

Bounded checks were limited to the existing packaged identifier metadata, one row from COMP.FUNDQ, the typed environment snapshot, frozen catalog lookups, and Python distribution metadata. No source row values were retained. Catalog and one-row metadata do not establish historical coverage, author extract identity or population completeness.

The verified COMP.FUNDQ route establishes a readable local quarterly product with the exact native fields needed by the CSV extraction stage; the required date coverage remains unverified. No author code, SAS startup, model fit, regression, installation, download, authentication test or external request was performed.

Only full_pipeline is assessed because the packaged Identifiers.parquet is an identifier subset rather than a prepared analysis panel. Tab2_ModelEval.py and Tab3_InnerWorkings.py are independent stages; create_sample.py produces CALL_LEVEL_SAMPLE.parquet for the market-outcome scripts; the two market-outcome source files have the same frozen content hash and should be run once.

The first complete Draft 2020-12 validation helper attempt failed during artifact hash verification because the preserved v1 field-comparison failure row had a one-character SHA-256 transcription error. The exact submitted input, helper source, combined diagnostic and value-only hash-classifier capture are preserved. The corrected digest now matches the actual JSON object; process-only evidence rows E_PROCESS_READER_V1, E_PROCESS_FIELD_V1, E_PROCESS_DRAFT_VALIDATOR_V2, E_PROCESS_HASH_CAPTURE_V1 and E_PROCESS_VALIDATOR_INPUT_V2 are deliberately unused in every evidence_ids list.

After correcting the process-only digest, the actual Draft202012Validator returned zero errors for the frozen output.schema.json. The saved v3 validation capture also checked nested typed IDs and dependency targets, every evidence_ids array, action coverage, exact source-consumed fields, JSON-object artifact shape and artifact hashes. This audit did not execute the author programs or verify analysis results.
